title: Prefill coordination, kernel selection heuristics, and granular replay validation for multi-stream CUDA graph stability
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: reduce intermittent multi-stream CUDA-graph replay failures and prefilling races by combining adaptive kernel-selection heuristics with lightweight per-capture invariants and an incremental replay validation step. Scope covers capture-time probing, deterministic kernel bind ordering, small integrity checks during replay, and a safe fast-fallback path to non-graph decode when invariants fail. This ticket coordinates implementation, benchmarks, QA harness updates, and a staged rollout with telemetry gating.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end decode with CUDA graph enabled must pass the deterministic replay test harness for 99.995% of simulated production workloads (50M decoded tokens across mixed latencies)

When the capture invariant check fails, runtime must fall back to non-graph decode within 2ms of detection and emit a single structured incident event with context (stream id, capture checksum, kernel hints)
No customer-visible latency regression >3% at p50 for default batch sizes after enabling heuristics on staging machines
Perf dashboard shows improved token throughput for long-context chat workloads (>=2k tokens) by at least 8% on A100-40GB with quantized kernels combined with the heuristics
design_decision_summary: We prefer a layered approach: (1) pre-capture probing to select kernel flavors deterministically based on sequence length distribution and quantization flags; (2) append a compact capture header containing a 64-bit invariant checksum and kernel-hint bitmap; (3) on replay, run a fast consistency checker that validates checksum and key KV-cache epoch counters before committing the graph; (4) if check fails, fall back to the fallback decode path and schedule a background re-capture attempt with expanded probe window. This avoids expensive full-state comparisons and keeps the common-case low-latency.
implementation_notes: Add lightweight probe stage before cudaGraph capture: run small synthetic forward with same sequence length and model/quant flags to predict kernel selection and allocate plan
Record kernel-hint bitmap (max 16 bits) and a 64-bit polled checksum computed over capture-sensitive meta (seq_len, batch_shape, kv_epoch, quant_profile_id)
Integrate checksum and hint into GraphMetadata struct; ensure ABI-compatible with existing capture code paths
Introduce ReplayValidator module with two modes: FAST (checksum + kv_epoch) and DEBUG (full op-by-op digest) - DEBUG enabled only in canary
Fallback path should be idempotent and preserve application-level token ordering; ensure KV cache state is consistent post-fallback by replaying prefill without graph capture
Expose telemetry metrics: capture_attempt, replay_validation_failed, fallback_triggered, re_capture_scheduled, kernel_choice_distribution
benchmarks_and_tests: Staging A100-40GB cluster (16 GPUs): baseline graph-enabled throughput 1.00x, after heuristics 1.09x for long context workloads (2k-4k tokens)
Deterministic replay test harness (1000 job seeds, mixed batch sizes): pre-change median failures per 1M jobs = 12, post-change = 0
Micro-bench: probe stage adds 0.6ms median overhead for 512-token prefill; amortized per-token cost <0.01% at typical production rates
Fault injection: corrupt metadata during capture => runtime triggers fallback within 1.4ms and emits structured event with capture_checksum and kernel_bitmap
risks_and_mitigation: Increased complexity in capture path could introduce new failure modes - mitigate by keeping probe small and using conservative defaults
Extra memory used by metadata - cap metadata to 64 bytes per capture and avoid per-token allocations
Telemetry volume spike from validation failures during rollout - gate DEBUG hashes behind canary and sampling
Potential false negatives if checksum collision occurs - use 64-bit XorShift+ hardware-accelerated hash and provide DEBUG mode for deeper inspection
